deficits.evidence: no purpose-built sidewalk on the right side of the road
deficits.suggestion: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the right side of the road to provide a safe space for pedestrians.

deficits.evidence: pedestrians are present and crossing demand exists but no designated crossing facility is provided
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing to safely facilitate movement across the road.

deficits.evidence: the kerb is not dropped at the crossing point
deficits.suggestion: Install dropped kerbs at the crossing point to improve accessibility for all users.

ratings.reason: The right side of the road lacks a dedicated footway, and building one is feasible.
Pedestrians are present but no marked crossing exists; adding one is a standard improvement.
The existing kerb is not dropped, hindering accessibility.
